meta.title: Team // MTLNOG
meta.description: The people who organize MTLNOG, the Montreal Network Operator Group.

eric.bio: Eric Dugas is a network architecture, engineering and operations leader and community builder in Montreal's Internet ecosystem, with almost 20 years of experience in the telecom industry across a range of service providers. He is Director, Network Operations at EBOX and Vice-Chair of CANIX (formerly QIX), the community-driven Internet exchange operator with exchanges in Montréal, Québec City, Ottawa and Toronto. Co-founder of MTLNOG, a non-profit organization founded in 2019 and federally incorporated in 2021 that now has over 110 members, Eric helps bring Montreal's network operators and engineers together to share knowledge, strengthen peering relationships and grow a stronger local Internet community.

jonathan.bio: Jonathan Senecal is a network operations leader and open-source developer in Montreal's Internet community. Driven by a personal mission to make things, fix stuff and help others, he is known among peers as a curious, self-taught problem solver and a generous mentor. With almost 20 years of experience in the telecom industry, he has designed and operated telecommunications networks for service providers across Canada and the northern US. He is Manager, Network Operations and Technology at Métro Optic and also runs Les Réseaux Loop Inc., a network infrastructure consulting firm. A former board member of QIX (now CANIX), he was also a core maintainer of NetBox, an open-source tool widely used by network operators around the world, and continues to contribute to it. As co-founder of MTLNOG, a federally incorporated non-profit that brings together over 110 network operators and engineers in the Montreal area, Jonathan helps organize its meetups and promotes knowledge sharing and collaboration across the community.

denis.bio: Denis Bonneau is a recognized leader in the telecommunications, digital infrastructure, and broadcast technology sectors. With more than 20 years of experience in business development and building technology communities, he recently joined MTLNOG as an Ad Hoc Director. Drawing on his experience with SMPTE, where he actively contributed to the growth and visibility of the Montreal/Quebec Section, Denis supports MTLNOG in developing its activities, strengthening its network of partners, and creating high-value events for Quebec's networking and Internet community.

meta.title: Sponsorship // MTLNOG
meta.description: Sponsor MTLNOG's in-person events in Montréal: sponsorship tiers, and where your support goes.

sponsorship.label: Sponsorship {year} · BBQ & meetings
sponsorship.heading: Support Montreal's network operator community
mission: MTLNOG is a non-profit organization established in 2019 with the aim of fostering coordination and collaboration among network operators in the greater Montreal area. Our mission is to facilitate knowledge sharing and professional development among networking professionals from diverse industries.

We strive to promote meaningful partnerships and collaborations among our members to address common challenges and achieve shared objectives in network operations. Additionally, we are dedicated to engaging with the broader community, including students and professionals in the IT field, to raise awareness about networking technologies and create a platform for community interaction, partnership and learning.

venue.label: Venue
venue.text: Have a space that could host network operators for an evening? We're looking for organizations that can provide a venue free of charge. Requirements such as capacity, A/V and location vary from event to event, and we'll work them out with you.

costs.label: Where your money goes
costs.intro: Sponsorship covers what it takes to run each event, for about 20–25 people, and to keep MTLNOG running. In short:

items.name: Food and drinks
items.text: Quality food and non-alcoholic beverages for attendees.

items.name: Logistics and coordination
items.text: Planning, equipment, supplies and on-site support, so each event runs smoothly.

items.name: Swag
items.text: Event t-shirts made with a local partner, and a second batch if enough sponsors join us. Everybody loves swag.

items.name: Operating expenses
items.text: The costs of keeping MTLNOG an incorporated non-profit: incorporation fees, insurance, accounting and infrastructure (hosting, domains and online services).

closing.heading: Partner with us
paragraphs: By participating in our sponsorship program, you will not only contribute to the success of our in-person events but also gain exposure and recognition within our community. Your generosity will help us continue organizing meaningful and engaging events for our participants.
Please let us know if you have any questions or require further information. We look forward to partnering with you to make our events a resounding success.
closing.note: Note: The proposed sponsorship program is subject to revision and customization based on individual sponsors' requirements and preferences.
